RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's composition is not evidence of anything. All-women panels are common in laboratory medicine and nursing-adjacent fields, and mixed panels show no reliable bias advantage either way. Raising it as your opening argument makes you look aggrieved rather than qualified, and it's easy to dismiss.

Your stronger ground is substantive: the appointee's qualifications appear lower than yours on paper, "broad leadership experience" is vague, and you've had no reply in two weeks. Send a firm written follow-up requesting the selection criteria, their weighting, and your scores against each. If the answer reveals criteria invented or reweighted after the fact, you have a real complaint — and then composition becomes context, not the case.
